nodes.name: $G(n,p)$ model
nodes.statement: The $G(n,p)$ model (Erdos-Renyi) is a random graph on $n$ vertices where each pair of distinct vertices is connected by an edge independently with probability $p$.

nodes.name: Increasing property
nodes.statement: A graph property $Q$ is increasing if whenever a graph $G$ has property $Q$, any graph obtained by adding edges to $G$ also has property $Q$.

nodes.name: Phase transition and threshold
nodes.statement: A property has a phase transition at threshold $p(n)$ if for $p_1(n) = o(p(n))$, $G(n,p_1)$ almost surely lacks the property, and for $p_2(n)/p(n) \to \infty$, $G(n,p_2)$ almost surely has it. If this holds for $cp(n)$ with $c<1$ vs $c>1$, the threshold is sharp.

nodes.name: Branching process
nodes.statement: A branching process generates a random tree: starting from a root, each node independently has children according to a fixed probability distribution. The generating function is $f(x) = \sum_{i=0}^{\infty} p_i x^i$.

nodes.name: Power law degree distribution
nodes.statement: A power law degree distribution is one where the number of vertices of degree $k$ scales as $cn/k^r$ for some constant $r > 0$, often slightly less than 3.

nodes.name: CNF formula and satisfiability
nodes.statement: A $k$-CNF formula over $n$ variables is an AND of clauses, each an OR of at most $k$ literals. A formula is satisfiable if there exists a truth assignment satisfying every clause.

nodes.name: Small world graph (Kleinberg model)
nodes.statement: An $n \times n$ grid with local edges to 4 neighbors plus one long-distance directed edge per vertex, where the probability of edge from $u$ to $v$ is proportional to $1/d^r(u,v)$ for parameter $r$.

nodes.name: Degree concentration in $G(n,p)$
nodes.statement: For vertex $v$ in $G(n,p)$ and $\alpha \in (0, \sqrt{np})$: $\mathrm{Pr}(|np - \deg(v)| \geq \alpha\sqrt{np}) \leq 3e^{-\alpha^2/8}$.
The degree is the sum of $n-1$ independent Bernoulli$(p)$ variables; apply the Master Tail Bounds (Theorem 12.6 in the appendix).
proof_strategy: tail bounds on sum of independent variables

nodes.name: All degrees concentrated
nodes.statement: If $p \geq 9\ln n/(n\varepsilon^2)$, then almost surely every vertex has degree in $[(1-\varepsilon)np, (1+\varepsilon)np]$.
conclusions: Almost surely every vertex has degree in $[(1-\varepsilon)np, (1+\varepsilon)np]$

nodes.statement: Apply Theorem 8.1 with $\alpha = \varepsilon\sqrt{np}$ to each vertex and take a union bound over $n$ vertices.

nodes.name: Second moment method
nodes.statement: If $x(n)$ is a nonneg. r.v. with $E(x) > 0$ and $\mathrm{Var}(x) = o(E^2(x))$, then $x$ is almost surely positive.
For $x \leq 0$, it must differ from $E(x)$ by at least $E(x)$. Apply Chebyshev: $\mathrm{Pr}(x \leq 0) \leq \mathrm{Var}(x)/E^2(x) \to 0$.

nodes.name: Second moment method (alternative form)
nodes.statement: If $E(x) > 0$ and $E(x^2) \leq E^2(x)(1+o(1))$, then $x$ is almost surely positive.
If $E(x^2) \leq E^2(x)(1+o(1))$, then $\mathrm{Var}(x) = E(x^2) - E^2(x) = o(E^2(x))$, so apply Theorem 8.3.

nodes.name: Sharp threshold for diameter two
nodes.statement: The property that $G(n,p)$ has diameter $\leq 2$ has a sharp threshold at $p = \sqrt{2}\sqrt{\ln n / n}$.
conclusions: For $p = c\sqrt{\ln n / n}$: if $c > \sqrt{2}$ then diameter $\leq 2$ a.s.; if $c < \sqrt{2}$ then diameter $> 2$ a.s.

nodes.statement: Count bad pairs (no common neighbor, not adjacent). For $c > \sqrt{2}$, $E(x) \to 0$ (first moment). For $c < \sqrt{2}$, $E(x^2) \leq E^2(x)(1+o(1))$ by splitting into cases $a=4,3,2$ distinct indices (second moment).

nodes.name: Sharp threshold for disappearance of isolated vertices
nodes.statement: The disappearance of isolated vertices in $G(n,p)$ has a sharp threshold at $p = \ln n / n$.
conclusions: For $p = c\ln n / n$: if $c > 1$ then no isolated vertices a.s.; if $c < 1$ then isolated vertices exist a.s.

nodes.statement: Let $x$ = number of isolated vertices. $E(x) = n(1-p)^{n-1} \approx n^{1-c}$. For $c > 1$, $E(x) \to 0$ (first moment). For $c < 1$, show $E(x^2)/E^2(x) \to 1$ using indicator variables (second moment via Corollary 8.4).

nodes.name: Explored set bounded after DFS queries
nodes.statement: In DFS on $G(n,(1+\varepsilon)/n)$, after $\varepsilon n^2/2$ edge queries, w.h.p. $|E| < n/3$.
If $|E| = n/3$ at time $t \leq \varepsilon n^2/2$, then $|F| \leq n/3$ w.h.p., so $|U| \geq n/3$. Then $|E||U| \geq n^2/9$ queries answered no, contradicting $t \leq n^2/16$.

nodes.name: Large frontier implies giant component
nodes.statement: In DFS on $G(n,(1+\varepsilon)/n)$, after $\varepsilon n^2/2$ edge queries, w.h.p. $|F| \geq \varepsilon^2 n/30$.

Suppose $|F| < \varepsilon^2 n/30$. The expected yes-answers exceed $\varepsilon n/2 + \varepsilon^2 n/3$, forcing $|E| \geq \varepsilon n/2 + 3\varepsilon^2 n/10$. Then $|E||U| > \varepsilon n^2/2$, a contradiction.

nodes.name: Threshold for cycles
nodes.statement: The threshold for the existence of cycles in $G(n,p)$ is $p = 1/n$ (not sharp).
conclusions: For $p = o(1/n)$, a.s. no cycles. For $p = d/n$ with $d > 1$, a.s. cycles exist.

nodes.statement: Count cycles: $E(x) = \sum_{k=3}^n \binom{n}{k}\frac{(k-1)!}{2}p^k \leq 2(np)^3$ for $np < 1/2$. For $np \to 0$, first moment gives no cycles. For $d \geq 1$, $E(x) \to \infty$ and second moment argument applies.

nodes.name: Expected number of size-$k$ components
nodes.statement: The expected number of connected components of size $k$ in $G(n,p)$ is at most $\binom{n}{k}k^{k-2}p^{k-1}(1-p)^{kn-k^2}$.
Union bound over $k^{k-2}$ spanning trees on $k$ vertices (Cayley's formula). Each tree has probability $p^{k-1}$ of being present, and $(1-p)^{k(n-k)}$ that no edge exits the component.

nodes.name: Giant component absorbs small components
nodes.statement: For $p = c\ln n / n$ with $c > 1/2$, a.s. only isolated vertices and a giant component remain. For $c > 1$, the graph is connected.
conclusions: $c > 1/2$: only isolated vertices and giant component

nodes.statement: Substitute $p = c\ln n/n$ into Lemma 8.10. Show $f(k) = \ln E(x_k)$ is maximized at $k=2$ with value $(1-2c)\ln n$. Sum over $k \in [2, n/2]$ gives $O(n^{1-2c}) \to 0$ for $c > 1/2$. Connectivity for $c > 1$ follows from Theorem 8.6.

nodes.name: Neighborhood growth in $G(n,p)$
nodes.statement: In $G(n,p)$ with $p = c\ln n/n$, if $|S_1| + \cdots + |S_i| \leq n/1000$, then $\mathrm{Pr}(|S_{i+1}| < 2(|S_1| + \cdots + |S_i|)) \leq e^{-10|S_i|}$.
$|S_{i+1}|$ is sum of independent Bernoulli r.v.s. Show $E(|S_{i+1}|) \geq 200|S_i|$ by concavity argument on $f(\alpha) = 1 - e^{-c\alpha\ln n} - 400\alpha$. Apply Chernoff bounds.

nodes.name: $O(\ln n)$ diameter
nodes.statement: For $p \geq c\ln n/n$ with $c$ sufficiently large, a.s. $G(n,p)$ has diameter $O(\ln n)$.

By Corollary 8.2, every vertex has degree $\Omega(\ln n)$. By Lemma 8.12, neighborhoods double each step, reaching $n/1000$ in $O(\ln n)$ steps. Two such sets of size $\geq n/1000$ have an edge between them w.h.p.

nodes.name: Monotonicity of increasing properties in $p$
nodes.statement: If $Q$ is an increasing property and $0 \leq p \leq q \leq 1$, then $\mathrm{Pr}(G(n,q) \text{ has } Q) \geq \mathrm{Pr}(G(n,p) \text{ has } Q)$.
Generate $G(n,q)$ as the union of $G(n,p)$ and $G(n,(q-p)/(1-p))$. Since $Q$ is increasing, if $G(n,p)$ has $Q$, so does the union.

nodes.name: Every increasing property has a threshold
nodes.statement: Each increasing property $Q$ of $G(n,p)$ has a phase transition at $p(n)$, the minimum value where $\mathrm{Pr}(G(n,p(n)) \text{ has } Q) = 1/2$.

Suppose $p_0(n)/p(n) \to 0$ but $\mathrm{Pr}(G(n,p_0) \in Q) \geq \varepsilon$ infinitely often. The $m$-fold replication ($m = \lceil 1/\varepsilon \rceil$) has $Q$ with prob $\geq 1/2$, giving $mp_0 \geq p(n)$, contradicting $p_0/p \to 0$.

nodes.name: Convergence of branching process iterates
nodes.statement: If $m = f'(1) > 1$ and $q$ is the unique root of $f(x) = x$ in $[0,1)$, then $\lim_{j \to \infty} f_j(x) = q$ for $x \in [0,1)$.
assumptions: $f(x) = \sum p_i x^i$ is the generating function

nodes.statement: For $x \leq q$: $x < f(x) < \cdots < q$, increasing and bounded. For $q \leq x < 1$: $x > f(x) > \cdots > q$, decreasing and bounded. Both converge to the fixed point $q$.

nodes.name: Extinction probability of branching process
nodes.statement: If the expected number of children $m \leq 1$, extinction probability is 1 (unless $p_1 = 1$). If $m > 1$, the extinction probability is the unique solution to $f(x) = x$ in $[0,1)$.
assumptions: Branching process with child generating function $f(x)$
conclusions: $m > 1$: extinction probability $= q$, the root of $f(x)=x$ in $[0,1)$

nodes.statement: For $m \leq 1$, convexity of $f$ implies $f(x) > x$ on $[0,1)$, so only root is $x=1$. For $m > 1$, $f'(1) > 1$ and convexity give a unique root $q < 1$. Apply Lemma 8.16.

nodes.name: Expected size of extinct families
nodes.statement: If $m = f'(1) \neq 1$, the expected size of an extinct family is $1/(1 - f'(q)) < \infty$. If $m = 1$ and $p_1 < 1$, the expected size is infinite.
By Bayes rule, $E(z_i | \text{extinction}) = (f'(q))^i$. Sum over generations: total size $= \sum_{i=0}^\infty (f'(q))^i = 1/(1-f'(q))$, which is finite since $f'(q) < 1$ when $m \neq 1$.

nodes.name: SC heuristic finds satisfying assignment
nodes.statement: If a random 3-CNF formula has $cn$ clauses with $c < 2/3$, then with probability $1-o(1)$ the Shortest Clause heuristic finds a satisfying assignment.
conclusions: SC heuristic finds a satisfying assignment w.h.p.

nodes.name: Independence of clause arrival times
nodes.statement: The times $T_i$ at which clause $i$ first becomes a 2-clause are mutually independent (by deferred decisions), and $\mathrm{Pr}(T_i = t) \leq 3/(2(n-2))$.

Use deferred decisions: clause contents are revealed only when needed. The probability that clause $i$ gets a negated literal at step $t$ is $(1/2)(3/(n-t+1))\prod(1-3/(n-j))$, which is at most $3/(2(n-2))$. Independence follows from clauses being handled independently.

nodes.name: Busy window bounded
nodes.statement: With probability $1-o(1)$, no clause remains a 2 or 1-clause for more than $O(\ln n)$ steps during SC.
conclusions: All busy windows have length $O(\ln n)$ w.h.p.

nodes.statement: The arrival rate of 2-clauses is $3c/2 < 1$. By Chernoff bounds, the probability that $> s-r$ clauses arrive in window $[r,s]$ of length $c_2\ln n$ is $\leq 1/n^3$. Union bound over $O(n^2)$ windows gives $o(1)$.

nodes.name: Expected triangles in $G(n,d/n)$
nodes.statement: The expected number of triangles in $G(n,d/n)$ is $d^3/6$, independent of $n$. For $d > \sqrt[3]{6}$, a triangle exists with nonzero probability.

nodes.name: Existence of giant component
nodes.statement: For $p = (1+\varepsilon)/n$ with $\varepsilon > 0$, $G(n,p)$ w.h.p. contains a giant component of size $\Omega(n)$, and all other components have size $O(\ln n)$.
conclusions: Giant component of size $\Omega(n)$ exists w.h.p.

nodes.name: No giant component below threshold
nodes.statement: When $p < 1/n$, w.h.p. all components in $G(n,p)$ have size $O(\ln n)$.
conclusions: All components have size $O(\ln n)$ w.h.p.

nodes.name: Threshold for Hamilton circuits
nodes.statement: The threshold for Hamilton circuits in $G(n,p)$ is $p = \ln n / n$, coinciding with the disappearance of degree-one vertices. The expected number of Hamilton circuits diverges at $p = e/n$ but the second moment method fails there.
conclusions: Threshold for Hamiltonian cycles is $p = \ln n / n$

nodes.name: Upper bound on SAT threshold
nodes.statement: For random $k$-CNF with $cn$ clauses, if $c > 2^k \ln 2$ then the formula is a.s. unsatisfiable. Thus $r_k \leq 2^k \ln 2$.

nodes.name: Molloy-Reed condition for giant component
nodes.statement: For a random graph with fraction $\lambda_i$ of degree-$i$ vertices, a giant component exists iff $\sum_{i=0}^{\infty} i(i-2)\lambda_i > 0$.
assumptions: Random graph with given degree distribution $\lambda_i$

nodes.name: Degree distribution of growth model without preferential attachment
nodes.statement: In the growth model (new vertex at each step, edge with prob $\delta$ to random pair), the degree distribution is $p_k = \frac{1}{1+2\delta}\left(\frac{2\delta}{1+2\delta}\right)^k$, exponentially decaying. The phase transition for a giant component occurs at $\delta = 1/8$.
assumptions: Growth model without preferential attachment, parameter $\delta$

nodes.name: Power law from preferential attachment
nodes.statement: In a growth model with preferential attachment (edge to vertex proportional to degree), the expected degree of vertex $i$ at time $t$ is $\delta\sqrt{t/i}$, yielding power law degree density $p(d) = 2\delta^2/d^3$.
assumptions: Growth model with preferential attachment, parameter $\delta$

nodes.name: Small world routing
nodes.statement: In Kleinberg's small world model: for $r = 2$, a greedy local algorithm finds paths of expected length $O((\ln n)^3)$; for $r < 2$, short $O(\ln n)$ paths exist but no local algorithm finds them in polylog time; for $r > 2$, no polylog paths exist.
assumptions: $n \times n$ grid with long-distance edges, parameter $r$
conclusions: $r<2$: $O(\ln n)$ paths exist, no local polylog algorithm

nodes.name: Shortest Clause (SC) Heuristic
nodes.statement: Repeatedly pick a shortest clause, set a random literal in it to true, delete satisfied clauses, and shrink clauses containing the negated literal. Fails if a 0-length clause is produced.
input: Random 3-CNF formula with $n$ variables and $cn$ clauses

nodes.name: DPLL solver
nodes.statement: Complete SAT solver: set pure literals, propagate unit clauses, then branch on a chosen literal recursively trying both truth values.
output: Satisfying assignment or proof of unsatisfiability

nodes.name: WalkSAT
nodes.statement: Incomplete local-search solver: start with random assignment, flip variables in unsatisfied clauses (greedy or random, chosen by coin flip), restart after $T_{\text{flips}}$ steps.

nodes.name: Greedy routing in small world ($r=2$)
nodes.statement: At each step, follow the edge (local or long-distance) whose endpoint is closest to the destination $t$. Expected path length is $O((\ln n)^3)$.
input: Source $s$, destination $t$ in $n \times n$ grid with $r=2$ long-distance edges

nodes.name: Degree distribution of $G(n,p)$
nodes.statement: $\mathrm{Pr}(\text{vertex has degree } k) = \binom{n}{k} p^k (1-p)^{n-k}$

nodes.name: Poisson approximation to binomial
nodes.statement: $\lim_{n \to \infty} \binom{n}{k} (d/n)^k (1-d/n)^{n-k} = d^k e^{-d} / k!$

nodes.name: Expected number of triangles
nodes.statement: $E(x) = \binom{n}{3} (d/n)^3 \approx d^3/6$

nodes.name: Triangle variance bound
nodes.statement: $\mathrm{Var}(x) = E(x^2) - E^2(x) \leq d^3/6 + o(1)$

nodes.name: Triangle existence by Chebyshev (Eq 8.1)
nodes.statement: $\mathrm{Pr}(x=0) \leq \mathrm{Var}(x)/E^2(x) \leq 6/d^3 + o(1)$

nodes.name: Expected bad pairs for diameter two
nodes.statement: $E(x) = \binom{n}{2}(1-p)(1-p^2)^{n-2} \approx (1/2) n^{2-c^2}$ for $p = c\sqrt{\ln n / n}$

nodes.name: Second moment partition for diameter two (Eq 8.2)
Expected isolated vertices
nodes.statement: $E(x) = n(1-p)^{n-1} \approx n^{1-c}$ for $p = c \ln n / n$

nodes.name: Expected number of cycles
nodes.statement: $E(x) = \sum_{k=3}^{n} \binom{n}{k} \frac{(k-1)!}{2} p^k \leq 2(np)^3$ for $np < 1/2$

nodes.name: Expected size-$k$ component count
nodes.statement: $E(x_k) \leq \binom{n}{k} k^{k-2} p^{k-1} (1-p)^{kn - k^2}$

nodes.name: Log expected components for connectivity proof
nodes.statement: $f(k) = \ln n + k + k \ln \ln n - 2 \ln k + k \ln c - ck \ln n + ck^2 \ln n / n$

nodes.name: Replication inequality (Eq 8.3)
nodes.statement: $\mathrm{Pr}(G(n,mp) \text{ has } Q) \geq \mathrm{Pr}(G(n,q) \text{ has } Q)$ where $q = 1-(1-p)^m \leq mp$

nodes.name: Branching process iteration
nodes.statement: $f_{j+1}(x) = f_j(f(x)) = \sum_{i=0}^{\infty} \mathrm{Pr}(z_j = i) f^i(x)$

nodes.name: Extinction probability as fixed point
nodes.statement: $q = \sum_{i=0}^{\infty} p_i q^i = f(q)$, i.e. $q$ is the root of $f(x) = x$

nodes.name: Expected generation size given extinction
nodes.statement: $E(z_i | \text{extinction}) = (f'(q))^i$

nodes.name: Expected extinct family size
nodes.statement: $\text{Expected size} = \sum_{i=0}^{\infty} (f'(q))^i = 1/(1 - f'(q))$

nodes.name: Clause arrival probability (SC)
nodes.statement: $\mathrm{Pr}(T_i = t) \leq 3/(2(n-2))$

nodes.name: Molloy-Reed condition
nodes.statement: $\sum_{i=0}^{\infty} i(i-2) \lambda_i > 0$ iff giant component exists

nodes.name: Molloy-Reed at $G(n,1/n)$
nodes.statement: $\sum_{i=0}^{\infty} i(i-2)/i! = \sum_{i=0}^{\infty} i^2/i! - 2\sum_{i=0}^{\infty} i/i! = 0$

nodes.name: Growth model degree distribution (Eq 8.5)
nodes.statement: $p_k = \frac{1}{1+2\delta} \left(\frac{2\delta}{1+2\delta}\right)^k$

nodes.name: Growth model degree recurrence (Eq 8.4)
nodes.statement: $d_k(t+1) = d_k(t) + 2\delta d_{k-1}(t)/t - 2\delta d_k(t)/t$

nodes.name: Growth model generating function ODE
nodes.statement: $g = -2\delta x g' + 2\delta x g g' + x$, equivalently $g' = (1/(2\delta)) (1 - g/x)/(1 - g)$

nodes.name: Growth model phase transition (Eq 8.6, 8.7)
nodes.statement: $g'(1) = (1 - \sqrt{1 - 8\delta})/(4\delta)$ for $\delta < 1/8$; $g'(1) = 1/(2\delta)$ for $\delta > 1/8$

nodes.name: Preferential attachment degree evolution
nodes.statement: $\partial d_i(t)/\partial t = d_i(t)/(2t)$, solution $d_i(t) = \delta \sqrt{t/i}$

nodes.name: Preferential attachment power law density
nodes.statement: $p(d) = 2\delta^2 / d^3$

nodes.name: Small world normalizing constant ($r=2$)
nodes.statement: $c_r(u) = \sum_v d^{-r}(u,v) \leq 4 \sum_{k=1}^{2n} 1/k = \Theta(\ln n)$ for $r = 2$

nodes.name: Small world hitting probability ($r=2$)
nodes.statement: $\mathrm{Pr}(\text{long edge from } u \text{ lands near } t) \geq \Omega(k^2 k^{-2}/\ln n) = \Omega(1/\ln n)$

nodes.name: Static giant component (growth model comparison)
nodes.statement: $S_{\text{static}} = 1 - 1/(\delta + \sqrt{\delta^2 + 2\delta})$ for $\delta > 1/4$; $S_{\text{static}} = 0$ for $\delta \leq 1/4$
The degree $\deg(v)$ equals $\sum_{i=1}^{n-1} x_i$ where $x_i$ are independent Bernoulli$(p)$ variables indicating edge presence.
Approximate $n-1 \approx n$ and apply the Master Tail Bound (Theorem 12.6) to the sum of independent random variables to obtain the stated concentration inequality.
Set $\alpha = \varepsilon \sqrt{np}$ in Theorem 8.1 to get $\mathrm{Pr}(|\deg(v) - np| \geq \varepsilon np) \leq 3 e^{-\varepsilon^2 np/8}$ for each vertex $v$.
Apply union bound: $\mathrm{Pr}(\text{some vertex outside range}) \leq 3n e^{-\varepsilon^2 np/8}$.
For $p \geq 9 \ln n/(n \varepsilon^2)$, the bound $3n e^{-\varepsilon^2 np/8} = o(1)$, proving all degrees are concentrated.
If $x \leq 0$, then $|x - E(x)| \geq E(x)$, so $\mathrm{Pr}(x \leq 0) \leq \mathrm{Pr}(|x - E(x)| \geq E(x))$.
By Chebyshev's inequality, $\mathrm{Pr}(|x - E(x)| \geq E(x)) \leq \mathrm{Var}(x)/E^2(x) \to 0$.
From $E(x^2) \leq E^2(x)(1+o(1))$, compute $\mathrm{Var}(x) = E(x^2) - E^2(x) \leq E^2(x) \cdot o(1) = o(E^2(x))$.
Apply Theorem 8.3 with $\mathrm{Var}(x) = o(E^2(x))$ to conclude $x$ is almost surely positive.
Define bad pair $(i,j)$: nonadjacent with no common neighbor. Let $x = \sum_{i<j} I_{ij}$. Diameter $\leq 2$ iff $x = 0$.
Compute $E(x) = \binom{n}{2}(1-p)(1-p^2)^{n-2} \approx (1/2) n^{2-c^2}$ for $p = c\sqrt{\ln n/n}$.
For $c > \sqrt{2}$: $E(x) \to 0$, so by first moment method, diameter $\leq 2$ a.s.
For $c < \sqrt{2}$: compute $E(x^2)$ by splitting into cases $a = 4, 3, 2$ distinct indices.
Case $a=3$: $E(I_{ij}I_{ik}) \leq n^{-2c^2}$; sum over triples gives $n^{3-2c^2}$.
Case $a=2$: $E(I_{ij}^2) = E(I_{ij})$, so sum equals $E(x)$.
Combine: $E(x^2) \leq (1/4) n^{4-2c^2} + n^{3-2c^2} + n^{2-c^2} \leq E^2(x)(1+o(1))$ for $c < \sqrt{2}$. Apply Corollary 8.4.
Let $x = \sum_{i=1}^n I_i$ where $I_i$ indicates vertex $i$ is isolated. Then $E(x) = n(1-p)^{n-1}$.
For $p = c \ln n / n$: $E(x) \approx n^{1-c}$. If $c > 1$, $E(x) \to 0$; first moment gives no isolated vertices a.s.
By Corollary 8.4, $\mathrm{Pr}(x = 0) \to 0$, so isolated vertices exist a.s. when $c < 1$.
Suppose at time $t \leq \varepsilon n^2/2$, $|E| = n/3$. Then $|F|$ is bounded by the sum of $\varepsilon n^2/2$ Bernoulli$(p)$ r.v.s.
W.h.p. $|F| \leq \varepsilon n^2 p \leq n/3$, so $|U| = n - |E| - |F| \geq n/3$.
All edges between $E$ and $U$ have been queried, so $|E||U| \geq n^2/9$ queries have been made. But $t \leq \varepsilon n^2/2 \leq n^2/16$, a contradiction.
Assume $|F| < \varepsilon^2 n/30$. Then $|U| \geq 1$ so DFS is active.
Expected yes-answers in $\varepsilon n^2/2$ queries is $p \varepsilon n^2/2 = (1+\varepsilon)\varepsilon n/2$. W.h.p. at least $\varepsilon n/2 + \varepsilon^2 n/3$ yes-answers.
So $|E| + |F| \geq \varepsilon n/2 + \varepsilon^2 n/3$, giving $|E| \geq \varepsilon n/2 + 3\varepsilon^2 n/10$.
$|E||U| \geq (\varepsilon n/2 + 3\varepsilon^2 n/10)(n - \varepsilon n/2 - \varepsilon^2 n/3) > \varepsilon n^2/2$, contradicting the query budget.
Count possible $k$-cycles: $\binom{n}{k}(k-1)!/2$ cycles of length $k$, each with probability $p^k$.
$E(x) = \sum_{k=3}^n \binom{n}{k}\frac{(k-1)!}{2} p^k \leq \sum_{k=3}^n (np)^k \leq 2(np)^3$ for $np < 1/2$.
For $p = o(1/n)$: $np \to 0$ so $E(x) \to 0$; first moment gives no cycles a.s.
For $d = 1$: $E(x) \geq (1/4) \sum_{k=3}^{\log n} 1/k \to \infty$. For $d > 1$, $E(x) \to \infty$ and second moment argument gives cycles a.s.
By Cayley's formula, there are $k^{k-2}$ spanning trees on $k$ labeled vertices.
Probability that a specific spanning tree is present: $p^{k-1}$. Probability no edge exits to remaining $n-k$ vertices: $(1-p)^{k(n-k)}$.
Union bound over $\binom{n}{k}$ vertex subsets and $k^{k-2}$ trees gives the bound $\binom{n}{k} k^{k-2} p^{k-1} (1-p)^{kn-k^2}$.
Substitute $p = c \ln n/n$ into Lemma 8.10 and simplify using $\binom{n}{k} \leq (en/k)^k$, $1-p \leq e^{-p}$.
Obtain $E(x_k) \leq \exp(f(k))$ where $f(k) = \ln n + k + k \ln \ln n - 2 \ln k + k \ln c - ck \ln n + ck^2 \ln n/n$.
$f''(k) > 0$, so $f$ is convex on $[2, n/2]$, maximized at endpoints. $f(2) \approx (1-2c) \ln n$, $f(n/2) \approx -cn \ln n/4$.
$E(\sum_{k=2}^{n/2} x_k) = O(n^{1-2c}) \to 0$ for $c > 1/2$. First moment method: no components of size $2$ to $n/2$ a.s.
For $c > 1$: connectivity follows from Theorem 8.6 (no isolated vertices at $c = 1$).

Construct $H$ as union of $G(n,p)$ and independent $G(n,(q-p)/(1-p))$. Edge probability in $H$: $p + (1-p)(q-p)/(1-p) = q$.
Since $Q$ is increasing and $G(n,p) \subseteq H$, whenever $G(n,p)$ has $Q$, so does $H \sim G(n,q)$.
Suppose $\mathrm{Pr}(G(n,p_0) \in Q) \geq \varepsilon$ on infinite set $I$ of $n$ values. Let $m = \lceil 1/\varepsilon \rceil$.
The $m$-fold replication $G(n,q)$ satisfies $\mathrm{Pr}(G(n,q) \notin Q) \leq (1-\varepsilon)^m \leq 1/e \leq 1/2$.
By monotonicity (Eq 8.3), $\mathrm{Pr}(G(n,mp_0) \in Q) \geq 1/2$, so $mp_0 \geq p(n)$, giving $p_0/p \geq 1/m$, contradicting $p_0/p \to 0$.
For $0 \leq x \leq q$: $x < f(x) \leq f(q) = q$, so $x < f_1(x) < f_2(x) < \cdots < q$, an increasing bounded sequence.
For $q \leq x < 1$: $f(q) \leq f(x) < x$, so $x > f_1(x) > f_2(x) > \cdots > q$, a decreasing bounded sequence.
Both sequences converge to a fixed point of $f$. Since $q$ is the unique fixed point in $[0,1)$, both converge to $q$.
If $m \leq 1$ (and $p_1 < 1$): $f$ is strictly convex with $f'(1) \leq 1$, so $f(x) > x$ for all $x \in [0,1)$. Only root is $x = 1$: extinction probability is 1.
If $m > 1$: $f'(1) > 1$ and convexity imply $f(x) = x$ has a unique root $q \in [0,1)$. By Lemma 8.16, $\lim f_j(x) = q$.
The limit generating function $\lim f_j(x) = q$ means $\mathrm{Pr}(z_j = 0) \to q$ and $\mathrm{Pr}(z_j = i) \to 0$ for finite $i > 0$. So extinction probability is $q$.
By Bayes rule: $\mathrm{Pr}(z_1 = k | \text{extinction}) = p_k q^{k-1}$. So $E(z_1 | \text{extinction}) = \sum k p_k q^{k-1} = f'(q)$.
By induction: $E(z_i | \text{extinction}) = (f'(q))^i$, using $z_i$ is sum of $z_{i-1}$ independent copies of $z_1$.
Total expected size $= \sum_{i=0}^{\infty} (f'(q))^i = 1/(1-f'(q))$. Since $f'(q) < 1$ when $m \neq 1$, the sum is finite.
Use deferred decisions: clause contents are revealed only when needed. At each step, pick a random variable and decide for each clause whether to include it.

In a busy window $[r+1, s]$, SC removes one 1/2-clause per step, so $\geq s-r$ new 2-clauses must have arrived.
By Lemma 8.20, clause arrival indicators are independent with total rate $\leq 3c(s-r)/2$ where $3c/2 < 1$.
By Chernoff, $\mathrm{Pr}(\text{arrivals} > s-r) \leq 1/n^3$ for $s - r = c_2 \ln n$. Union bound over $O(n^2)$ windows gives $o(1)$.
